newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed mostly higher following a stronger New York market. Front month November remained flat at $1,524, while January firmed $10 to close at $1,394. The market was awaiting latest US certified stock data due to be released after New York's close on Monday. Most expected a further draw on stocks while others said it could show a slight rise to reflect an adjustment following the reporting error. The market was not overly concerned by the situation in Zaire where fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairian troops have uprooted half a million people. Zaire is not a leading player on the market with exports in 1995/96 (October/September) estimated at 730,000 60-kg bags, down from 1.3 million bags the previous year. In New York arabica futures ended sharply higher. December added 3.10 cents/lb to close at 119.10 cents/lb, while March firmed 1.75 cents/lb to close at 105.85 cents/lb. This led to an increase in the December/March spread to 13.25 cents/lb, the result of nearby tightness. US certified coffee stocks declined by 4,036 bags to 1,547 bags so that only a handful of coffee is now left in storage. The exchange did make an adjustment upwards in one New Orleans warehouse of 150 bags following last week's announcement that a mistake was made in the counting. The differences, however, are so negligible that the error did not have any impact on prices. Many believe that certified coffee stocks will head down to zero and given the drawdown this week this seems to be the case, especially as there was no coffee pending grading. The drawdown in US certified coffee stocks comes at a time when exchange and non-exchange consumer stocks housed in US warehouses fell in September to 1.611 million bags, their lowest level since the Green Coffee Association of New York began tracking inventories in January 1988. Trade sources said that the situation seems to be so tight that it cannot get any tighter right now. However, when new supplies will be available in larger quantities, the December/March spread will come under pressure.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 4,036 bags to 1,547 bags during the week ended October 25. In New York stocks fell by 4,000 bags to 61 bags, while stocks in New Orleans declined marginally by 36 bags to 1,217 bags. Stocks in San Francisco and Miami remained unchanged at 250 and 19 bags respectively.

UNITED STATES - US coffee roastings for the week ended October 19 totalled 460,000 60-kg bags, up from 320,000 bags the previous week and compared with 405,000 in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 13.725 million bags vs 13.350 million bags in the same year-ago period.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong imported 19,598 bags of coffee in August 1996, 82 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 121,980 bags, 13 percent more than was imported in January/August 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell to 156,400 bags, down from 240,100 bags the previous year. Hong Kong gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from China and South Korea. Exports in January/August 1996 totalled 44,300 bags, 46 percent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped to 121,000 bags, down from 227,000 bags the previous year.

TAIWAN - Taiwan imported 23,542 bags of coffee in July 1996. This brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 120,525 bags. Taiwan gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles. South Korea supplied 27,000 bags of solubles in January/July 1996, while Singapore shipped 12,700 bags.
